The objectives of this notebook will be to conduct a cluster analysis on each sample's BLM predictor variables to identify a typological classification of samples. This classification will be balled Typology2

This will be conducted under the baseline BLM assumptions (HA 10% Closed System) within the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet Clean version 2.

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/5. Cluster analysis")
```

# Identifying Stream Typologies

Cluster analysis of all sites in WaDE Synoptic Survey

Import dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

head(dat)
```

First, we'll omit pooled samples

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  filter(Flow_state != "Pooled")

str(dat$Flow_state)
```

## 1. Select variables

We'll use the scaled, log-transformed BLM predictors to conduct a PCA

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Variables to select
vars_to_select <- c("log_Temp_C", "pH", "log_DOC_uM",
                    "log_DIC_uM", "log_Cl_uM", "log_Ca_uM", 
                    "log_Mg_uM", "log_SO4_uM", "log_Na_uM", 
                    "log_K_uM", "log_Zn_uM", "log_Cu_uM")

# Scale these variables
scaled_blm_predict <- as.data.frame(
  scale(dat[vars_to_select])
)

# Peek
head(scaled_blm_predict)
```

## 2. K-means clustering

### i. Identifying the number of clusters

Run k-means using 2-5 and identify which number of clusters minimizes the overlap

```{r}
library(cluster)
library(dplyr)

# Silhouette check for k = 2:5
set.seed(123)

sil_df <- lapply(2:10, function(k) {
  
  km <- kmeans(
    scaled_blm_predict,
    centers = k,
    nstart = 50
  )
  
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(scaled_blm_predict))
  
  data.frame(
    k = k,
    mean_silhouette = mean(sil[, 3])
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

sil_df
```

### ii. Clustering

Run k-means using 4 clusters

```{r}
# Run k-means
set.seed(123)
kmeans_result <- kmeans(scaled_blm_predict, centers = 4, nstart = 50)

# Add cluster labels to your data
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster))

# Check
str(dat$cluster)
```

## 4. Plot of clusters on PCA

Overlay clusters on PCA

```{r}
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0) Force cluster order + set cluster colors
#-------------------------------------------------
cluster_colors <- c(
  "4" = "#56B4E9",
  "1" = "#D55E00",
  "3" = "#999999",
  "2" = "#009E73"
)

# Force correct ordering
cluster_for_plot <- dat$cluster %>%
  factor(levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4"))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1) PCA
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_result <- prcomp(scaled_blm_predict, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_summary <- summary(pca_result)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2) PCA biplot (same depiction as your original)
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_cluster <- fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_result,
  geom.ind     = "point",
  col.var      = "black",
  habillage    = cluster_for_plot,
  addEllipses  = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Cluster",
  palette      = cluster_colors
) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Biplot of All Sites by Cluster",
    x = "PC1 (46.5%)",
    y = "PC2 (19.2%)"
  )

# View
pca_cluster

# Define output directory
out_dir <- "Identifying Typology Plots"
# Create directory if it does not exist
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "PCA_Biplot_All_Sites_by_Cluster.png"),
  plot     = pca_cluster,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

Variable loadings

```{r}
loadings_pc1_pc2 <- as.data.frame(pca_result$rotation[, c("PC1", "PC2")]) %>%

# View loadings
loadings_pc1_pc2

# Save 
library(openxlsx)
```

## 5. Characterizing clusters

### i. Frequency table

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# inherent characteristics 
site_char <- c("Type", "Regime", "Development")

cluster_summary_table_pct <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(site_char), cluster) %>%  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -cluster,        
    names_to = "Variable",  
    values_to = "Value"     
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, cluster, Value, name = "Freq") %>% 
  group_by(Variable, cluster) %>%          
  mutate(RelFreq = prop.table(Freq) * 100)       

cluster_summary_table_pct
```

Save table

```{r}
out_dir <- "Identifying Typology2 Plots"

library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  cluster_summary_table_pct,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Relative_freq_percentages_by_cluster.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

```

### ii. Plot of relative frequencies

```{r}
library(dplyr)
# Combine variable and value
cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_summary_table_pct %>%
  mutate(Value_labeled = paste0(Variable, ": ", Value))

# Change the order of Variable Values
cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled,
  levels = c(
    "Type: Tributaries",
    "Type: Main Stem",
    
    "Development: Low",
    "Development: Medium",
    "Development: High",
    
    "Regime: NonPerennial",
    "Regime: Perennial"
  )
)


# Create a named color vector for all Value_labeled combinations
color_map <- c(
  "Type: Tributaries" = "#dadaeb",
  "Type: Main Stem" = "#756bb1",
  
  "Development: Low" = "#fdd49e",
  "Development: Medium" = "orange2",
  "Development: High" = "red3",
  
  "Regime: NonPerennial" = "lightblue",
  "Regime: Perennial" = "#1f78a4"
)

# Modify the legend to only display the categorical value
legend_labels <- gsub("^.*: ", "", levels(cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled))

# Plot
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

rel_freq <- ggplot(cluster_summary_table_pct, 
       aes(y = Variable, x = RelFreq, fill = Value_labeled)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Relative Frequency (%)", y = NULL, fill = "Category") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
  strip.placement = "outside",
  strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
  panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
  legend.position = "right",        # move to right
  legend.box = "vertical",          # keep vertical layout
  legend.direction = "vertical"     # vertical legend
) +
guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) + # 1 column
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = color_map,
    labels = legend_labels)

rel_freq

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Relative_freq_plots_by_cluster.png"),
  plot     = rel_freq,
  width    = 6,
  height   = 4,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

-   Cluster 1: Highly developed perennial tributary sites

-   Cluster 2: Non-perennial tributary sites

-   Cluster 3: Mostly main stem sites

-   Cluster 4: Perennial tributary sites

### iii. Rename clusters to typologies

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster)) %>%
  mutate(cluster = dplyr::recode(
    cluster,
    `4` = "P Tribs",
    `1` = "PD Tribs",
    `3` = "Main Stem",
    `2` = "NP Tribs"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Typology = cluster) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Typology = as.factor(Typology)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Typology = factor(Typology, 
                          levels = c("NP Tribs",
                                     "P Tribs",
                                     "PD Tribs",
                                     "Main Stem")))

# check
levels(dat$Typology)
```

Save Typology column to Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx and save in current working directory

```{r}
#-------------------------------------------
# 1. Read in file
#-------------------------------------------
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx"

sheet_name <- "HA 10% Closed System"

ha10_dat <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name)

#-------------------------------------------
# 2. Build Typology lookup
#-------------------------------------------

typology_lookup <- dat %>%
  select(Sample_ID, Typology) %>%
  distinct()

#-------------------------------------------
# 3. Remove pooled samples from the imported
#    Excel sheet and add Typology
#-------------------------------------------

ha10_dat_updated <- ha10_dat %>%
  semi_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

#-------------------------------------------
# 4. Checks
#-------------------------------------------

unique(ha10_dat_updated$Typology) # Ensure it exists
unique(ha10_dat_updated$Flow_state) # Should only be Flowing

#-------------------------------------------
# 5. Save updated workbook in working directory
#    by REPLACING the target sheet
#-------------------------------------------
library(writexl)

write_xlsx(
  list("HA 10% Closed System" = ha10_dat_updated),
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx")
)
```

### a. Identify Sites with \>1 Typology Assignment

```{r}
# Determine which sites fall into more than 1 typology
sites_multiple_typology <- dat %>%
  distinct(Site, Typology) %>%        # unique Site–Typology pairs
  group_by(Site) %>%                  
  summarise(
    n_typologies = n(),               
    typologies = paste(sort(Typology), collapse = ", ")
  ) %>%
  filter(n_typologies > 1)            # keep sites with >1 typology

sites_multiple_typology

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Create workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# Add worksheets and write data
addWorksheet(wb, "Sites")
writeData(wb, "Sites", sites_multiple_typology)

# Save workbook
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Sites_with_many_typologies.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE)
```

### c. Dominant Typology for each Site

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Count observations per Site × Typology
site_typology_counts <- dat %>%
  group_by(Network, Site, Typology) %>%
  summarise(n_obs = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Determine dominant Typology per Site
site_dominant <- site_typology_counts %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = n_obs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  rename(Dominant_Typology = Typology,
         Dominant_n = n_obs) %>%
  ungroup()

# Join back for full site-level table
site_summary_table <- site_typology_counts %>%
  left_join(site_dominant %>%
              dplyr::select(Network, Site, Dominant_Typology),
            by = c("Network", "Site")) %>%
  arrange(Network, Site, desc(n_obs))

# Merged table
nested_table <- site_summary_table %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  summarise(
    Typologies_Observed = paste0(Typology, " (n=", n_obs, ")", collapse = "; "),
    Dominant_Typology   = first(Dominant_Typology),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Dominant_Typology = factor(Dominant_Typology)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Dominant_Typology, Network, Site)

nested_table

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  nested_table,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Sites_by_network_typology.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```
